summary: A six-turn office-automation session chains a spreadsheet edit (T1), an email draft/send to Ethan (T2), a calendar event + note to Priya (T3), a second Priya calendar event + update to Ethan (T4), and a sprawling six-part confirmation touching Ethan's inbox, the original email, a new event, a final Priya email, and re-reads (T5), before a wind-down (T6). The agent's one genuinely sharp move is at T1, where it flags that the workbook sheet is named Products, not Inventory as the user said, and reconciles the discrepancy. From T2 onward the run is a cascade of confident, fully-formatted confirmations — email bodies, calendar tables, inbox listings — none of which the component_timeline grounds in a retrieval tool (only generic other calls fire). As a CONTROL baseline, two uncorrected defects persist: the agent silently switches the email domain between @company.com (in "context reviewed") and @example.com (in "email sent") within the same turn, and claims to have "re-read" and "reviewed" threads that no retrieval call backs. The closing T5 self-asserts the coordination trail is "consistent end to end" — a circular verification against its own unverified outputs.
